finding_dispositions.note: Both article-text extractions were reopened and their digests matched their own artifact.toml values (Matthew 3d9a35cc..., 64,011 bytes; Daniel ab2fefc0..., 36,621 bytes). Matthew (Jacquier, CE vol. 10, 1911) was read at its own section 'Destination of the Gospel' (lines 195-197: the Fathers 'agree in declaring that St. Matthew wrote his Gospel for the Jews'; Origen's 'published for Jews converted to the Faith'; Jerome 'published his Gospel in Judea ... principally for those among the Jews who believed in Jesus'; Zahn's contrary qualification), at line 175 ('before his departure from Jerusalem') and at line 221 (the Biblical Commission on the native language of the Jews then in Palestine). Daniel (Gigot, CE vol. 4, 1908) was read at the intrinsic grounds, lines 19, 37, 43 and 45: 'a resident in Babylon', 'owing to his position at the court of Babylon', writing 'for the comfort of the Jews of his time and of subsequent ages', for readers at home in Hebrew and Aramaic. Negative results are recorded too: the Matthew article reports no rival place of composition (searched for Antioch, Syria and Alexandria), and the Daniel article gives the later author it reports no place of writing at all. Scope 7.6 keeps the writer's place, the first hearers, the narrated event's place and the critical horizon apart, and 7.4 forbids carrying any figure across from the articles' date sections; the one place clause inside Matthew's date section (line 201) is named and not used. In sections/80-date-location.tex the Gospel Location cell now reads 'Matthew in Judea, before he left Jerusalem; to the Jews who had believed. Event: the Temple, Jerusalem (21:23)' and its prose row carries the article's wording in place of 'No first audience is recorded'; the Offertory cell and prose row gained the same two fields. The study builds (38 physical pages, inside 20-50), and the twelve study-preflight checks plus the research-phase check, source-library validate and the research seal all pass.

notes: Records written, all inside the leaf: research/scope.md (new 7.6; revised head note, 7.3, 7.4, 5.2 and 10), research/source-bindings.toml (loci and context on the three Catholic Encyclopedia article-text bindings) and research/interpretations.md (head note and 2.6). One study file was edited, sections/80-date-location.tex, because STU-002's required_result names it: the dossier must carry what the record now holds. review-dependencies.toml is unchanged and still correct - every source read on this reentry is bound by source ID, so nothing new lies outside the seal. Three things the next stages should know. (1) The dossier appendix now runs to two physical pages (33-34) where the author had tightened it to one; the content is required by STU-002 and scope 7.6 says so, so the layout, not the fields, is what may be revised, and research/production-review.md still says 37 pages and one dossier page, which the author stage owns and must refresh. (2) A find of this reentry, recorded in scope 7.6 and carried in one clause of the Epistle's explanatory row: the same 1909 Catholic Encyclopedia article the leaf binds for the Epistle's date holds 'en Epheso' at 1:1 to be no part of the primitive text and reads the letter as a circular to churches Paul did not know. The dossier's 'to the saints at Ephesus (1:1)' is the received text (Clementine 'omnibus sanctis qui sunt Ephesi', Douay 'to all the saints who are at Ephesus', both re-read at 1:1); the critical view is now stated beside it as the profile's required modern horizon, and no figure was taken from those sentences. (3) Advisory STU-005's research half is cleared: interpretations.md 2.6 said Theodoret 'is not one of this reading's witnesses', contradicting that file's own 2.2, 2.5 and head note; it now states what he contributes to reading 2 (the non-distributive reading of Eph 4:6, with Chrysostom) and what he may not be credited with. The other half - the son-and-lord-of-david lane's author list in proper-components.toml, which omits him - is the study's file and is left to the author stage. Advisories STU-003 (Gregory's parable does not stand just before this Gospel) and STU-004 (the sentence about what the study declines to conclude from the Missal's typography) are study prose in sections/20 and sections/30 and were left untouched; the research record is already correct at both points. Remaining limitations: the traditional testimonies are carried as the encyclopedia's report and were not read at the Fathers' own loci (scope 10.9); no first audience or place of composition is held for the four psalms and none was sought beyond the titles and the corpus (scope 7.6, 5.2); and the earlier bounds of scope 5.2 and 10 stand.
summary: Research's fourth reentry for the Claude leaf 57-seventeenth-after-pentecost repaired STU-002. The traditional first audience and place of composition of the Gospel and of the Offertory's book were read on this stage's own loci in the two Catholic Encyclopedia articles this leaf already binds - away from their date sections - and are recorded in a new research/scope.md section 7.6, with the reading in 7.3, the bound on their use in 7.4, the article loci in research/source-bindings.toml and the limits in 5.2 and 10. The Gospel and Offertory dossiers in sections/80-date-location.tex now carry them as the Epistle dossier carries its own, and no passage's dossier reports a required field as unrecorded. No date, era or reign was added: chronology-claims-supported still reports seven Date cells, seven generated annotations and no direct chronology claim.
